1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None)``, ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals,
6	costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None,
7	snapshot=False, max_cost=None)``,
8	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
9	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)``,
10	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)``,
12	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
13	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
14	and
15	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
16	trace=False)``.
17	
18	Semantics:
19	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
20	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
21	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
22	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
23	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
24	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
25	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
26	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
27	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
28	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
29	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
30	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
31	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
32	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
33	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
34	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
35	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
36	
37	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
38	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
39	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
40	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
41	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
42	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
43	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
44	  check) and before the search starts.
45	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
46	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
47	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
48	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
49	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
50	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
51	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
52	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
53	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
54	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
55	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
56	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
57	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
58	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
59	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
60	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
61	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
62	  accepts no budget parameter.
63	
64	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
65	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
66	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
67	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
68	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
69	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
70	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
71	  starts.
72	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
73	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
74	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
75	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
76	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
77	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
78	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
79	  comparison or trace entries.
80	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
81	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
82	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
83	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
84	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
85	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
86	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
87	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
88	  rules are unchanged.
89	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
90	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
91	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
92	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
93	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
94	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
95	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
96	
97	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
98	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
99	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
100	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
101	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
102	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
103	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
104	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
105	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
106	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
107	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
108	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
109	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
110	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
111	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
112	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
113	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
114	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
115	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
116	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
117	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
118	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
119	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
120	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
121	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
122	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
123	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
124	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
125	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
126	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
127	
128	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
129	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
130	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
131	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
132	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
133	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
134	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
135	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
136	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
137	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
138	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
139	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
140	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
141	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
142	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
143	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
144	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
145	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
146	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
147	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
148	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
149	  other arrival times still compete.
150	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
151	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
152	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
153	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
154	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
155	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
156	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
157	  better route with a worse one.
158	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
159	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
160	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
161	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
162	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
163	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
164	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
165	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
166	  and step count.
167	
168	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
169	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
170	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)`` returns
171	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
172	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
173	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
174	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
175	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
176	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
177	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
178	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
179	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
180	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
181	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). Every error is
182	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
183	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
184	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
185	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
186	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
187	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
188	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
189	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
190	  sequences always remain separate results.
191	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
192	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
193	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
194	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
195	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
196	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
197	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
198	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
199	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
200	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
201	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
202	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
203	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
204	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
205	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
206	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
207	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
208	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
209	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
210	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
211	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
212	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
213	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
214	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
215	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
216	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
217	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
218	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
219	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
220	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
221	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
222	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
223	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
224	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
225	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
226	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
227	  value exactly unchanged.
228	
229	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
230	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
231	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
232	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
233	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
234	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
235	  included) and before the search starts.
236	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
237	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
238	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
239	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
240	  carry the field.
241	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
242	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
243	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
244	  provided), the closed-node count, the
245	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
246	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
247	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
248	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
249	  back to ``resume`` later.
250	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
251	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
252	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
253	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
254	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
255	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
256	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
257	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
258	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
259	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
260	  closed node twice.
261	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
262	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
263	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
264	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
265	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
266	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
267	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
268	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
269	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
270	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
271	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
272	
273	Offline replay (``replay``):
274	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
275	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
276	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
277	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
278	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
279	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
280	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
281	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
282	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
283	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
284	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
285	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
286	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
287	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
288	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
289	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
290	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
291	  ``start == goal``.
292	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
293	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
294	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
295	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
296	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
297	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
298	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
299	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
300	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
301	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
302	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
303	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
304	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
305	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
306	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
307	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
308	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
309	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
310	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
311	  ever returned.
312	
313	Distance field (``distance_field``):
314	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
315	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
316	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
317	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
318	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
319	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
320	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
321	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
322	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
323	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
324	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
325	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
326	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
327	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
328	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
329	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
330	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
331	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
332	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
333	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
334	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
335	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
336	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
337	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
338	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
339	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
340	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
341	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
342	
343	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
344	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
345	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
346	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
347	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
348	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
349	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
350	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
351	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
352	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
353	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
354	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
355	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
356	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
357	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
358	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
359	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
360	  the input permutation never changes any result.
361	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
362	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
363	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
364	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
365	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
366	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
367	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
368	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
369	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
370	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
371	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
372	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
373	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
374	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
375	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
376	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
377	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
378	  JSON-serializable.
379	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
380	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
381	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
382	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
383	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
384	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
385	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
386	
387	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
388	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
389	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
390	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
391	  normalized to tuples.
392	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
393	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
394	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
395	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
396	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
397	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
398	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
399	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
400	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
401	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
402	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
403	"""
404

420	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

423	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
424	    if not _is_int(value):
425	        raise TypeError(
426	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
427	        )
428	    if value <= 0:
429	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {value}")

433	def _normalize_point(value, name):
434	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
435	        raise TypeError(
436	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
437	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
438	        )
439	    if len(value) != 2:
440	        raise TypeError(
441	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
442	        )
443	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
444	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
445	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
446	    return (x, y)

450	    x, y = point

457	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
458	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
459	        raise TypeError(
460	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
461	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
462	        )
463	    cells = set()
464	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
465	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
466	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
467	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
468	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
469	    return cells

472	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
473	    if costs is None:
474	        return None  # unit step cost
475	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
476	        raise TypeError(
477	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
478	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
479	        )
480	    if len(costs) != height:
481	        raise ValueError(
482	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
483	        )
484	    rows = []
485	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
486	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
487	            raise TypeError(
488	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
489	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
490	            )
491	        if len(row) != width:
492	            raise ValueError(
493	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
494	                f"got {len(row)}"
495	            )
496	        parsed = []
497	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
498	            if not _is_int(cell):
499	                raise TypeError(
500	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
501	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
502	                )
503	            if cell <= 0:
504	                raise ValueError(
505	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
506	                    f"got {cell}"
507	                )
508	            parsed.append(cell)
509	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
510	    return tuple(rows)

513	def _normalize_dynamic_blocked(dynamic_blocked, width, height):
514	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
515	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
516	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
517	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
518	    ):
519	        raise TypeError(
520	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
521	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"
522	        )
523	    if len(dynamic_blocked) == 0:
524	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
525	    frames = []
526	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_blocked):
527	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Iterable):
528	            raise TypeError(
529	                f"dynamic_blocked[{t}] must be an iterable of grid "
530	                f"coordinates, got {type(frame).__name__}"
531	            )
532	        cells = set()
533	        for index, item in enumerate(frame):
534	            name = f"dynamic_blocked[{t}][{index}]"
535	            point = _normalize_point(item, name)
536	            _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
537	            cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
538	        frames.append(frozenset(cells))
539	    return frames

543	    if (path is None or isinstance(path, (str, bytes))
544	            or not isinstance(path, Sequence)):

560	def _normalize_goals(goals):
561	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
562	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
563	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``
564	    # and other non-sequences are ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a
565	    # ``ValueError``; every element is normalized to a coordinate tuple
566	    # (element shape/coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``). Bounds and
567	    # obstacle checks follow in ``plan_any`` at the same relative positions
568	    # ``plan`` uses for its single goal. Duplicates merge and the tuple is
569	    # sorted so the input order never affects the result.
570	    if (goals is None or isinstance(goals, (str, bytes))
571	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):
572	        raise TypeError(
573	            f"goals must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
574	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"
575	        )
576	    if len(goals) == 0:
577	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
578	    points = set()
579	    for index, item in enumerate(goals):
580	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")
581	        points.add(point)
582	    return tuple(sorted(points))

626	def _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited):
627	    # The failure status when a limit is in play: a budget stop always
628	    # wins, then a cost-limit discard, otherwise plain unreachability.
629	    if budget_stop:
630	        return "budget_exhausted"
631	    if cost_limited:
632	        return "cost_exhausted"
633	    return "unreachable"

636	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
637	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False, state=None):
638	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
639	
640	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
641	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
642	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
643	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
644	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
645	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
646	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
647	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
648	    uninterrupted call. With
649	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
650	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
651	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
652	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
653	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
654	    """
655	
656	    def heuristic(point):
657	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
658	
659	    def step_cost(point):
660	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
661	        if costs is None:
662	            return 1
663	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
664	
665	    if state is None:
666	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
667	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
668	        # is never compared.
669	        h0 = heuristic(start)
670	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
671	        came_from = {}
672	        g_score = {start: 0}
673	        closed = set()
674	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
675	        cost_limited = False
676	    else:
677	        open_heap = state["open"]
678	        came_from = state["came_from"]
679	        g_score = state["g_score"]
680	        closed = state["closed"]
681	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
682	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
683	    budget_stop = False
684	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
685	
686	    while open_heap:
687	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
688	        current = entry[4]
689	        if current in closed:
690	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
691	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
692	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
693	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
694	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
695	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
696	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
697	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
698	            budget_stop = True
699	            if snapshot:
700	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
701	            break
702	        closed.add(current)
703	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
704	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
705	        if current == goal:
706	            path = [current]
707	            while path[-1] in came_from:
708	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
709	            path.reverse()
710	            result = {
711	                "path": path,
712	                "cost": g_score[current],
713	                "expanded": len(closed),
714	            }
715	            if has_status:
716	                result["status"] = "found"
717	            if trace:
718	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
719	            return result
720	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
721	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
722	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
723	                continue
724	            if nxt in obstacles:
725	                continue
726	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
727	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
728	                if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
729	                    # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
730	                    # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
731	                    cost_limited = True
732	                    continue
733	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
734	                came_from[nxt] = current
735	                h = heuristic(nxt)
736	                heapq.heappush(
737	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
738	                )
739	    result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": len(closed)}
740	    if has_status:
741	        result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
742	    if trace:
743	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
744	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
745	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
746	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
747	            max_cost, len(closed), expanded_nodes,
748	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed,
749	                                   cost_limited, max_cost),
750	        )
751	    return result
752

754	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
755	                    trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
756	                    state=None):
757	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
758	
759	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
760	    past the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting in place and repeated
761	    coordinates are forbidden, so whether a candidate route can be
762	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
763	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
764	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
765	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
766	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
767	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
768	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
769	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
770	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
771	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
772	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
773	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
774	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
775	    state). With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally
776	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
777	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
778	    """
779	
780	    def heuristic(point):
781	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
782	
783	    def step_cost(point):
784	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
785	        if costs is None:
786	            return 1
787	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
788	
789	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1
790	
791	    def frame_cells(t):
792	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
793	
794	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
795	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
796	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
797	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
798	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
799	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
800	    if state is None:
801	        h0 = heuristic(start)
802	        start_path = (start,)
803	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
804	                      frozenset(start_path))]
805	        closed_count = 0
806	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
807	        cost_limited = False
808	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
809	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
810	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
811	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
812	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
813	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
814	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
815	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or
816	        # less) can remain undiscovered.
817	        best_key = None
818	    else:
819	        open_heap = state["open"]
820	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
821	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
822	        best_key = state["best_key"]
823	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
824	    budget_stop = False
825	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
826	
827	    while open_heap:
828	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
829	            break
830	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
831	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
832	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
833	            budget_stop = True
834	            break
835	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
836	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
837	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
838	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,
839	            # in the order their route nodes are actually closed.
840	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t))
841	        if (x, y) == goal:
842	            goal_key = (g, t, path)
843	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:
844	                best_key = goal_key
845	            continue  # routes end at the goal; never expanded past it
846	        next_t = t + 1
847	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
848	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
849	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
850	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
851	                continue
852	            nxt = (nx, ny)
853	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:
854	                continue  # static obstacle, timed obstacle, or revisit
855	            new_g = g + step_cost(nxt)
856	            if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
857	                # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
858	                # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
859	                cost_limited = True
860	                continue
861	            new_path = path + (nxt,)
862	            h = heuristic(nxt)
863	            heapq.heappush(
864	                open_heap,
865	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
866	                 seen | {nxt}),
867	            )
868	    if best_key is None:
869	        result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": closed_count}
870	        if has_status:
871	            result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
872	    else:
873	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
874	        result = {
875	            "path": list(best_path),
876	            "cost": best_g,
877	            "expanded": closed_count,
878	        }
879	        if has_status:
880	            result["status"] = "found"
881	    if trace:
882	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
883	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
884	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
885	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, frames,
